title: Honey Cake (1855)
author: A Lady of Philadelphia
description: An American honey cake recorded in 1855, richly flavoured with cinnamon and cream.
method: Cream butter and sugar together.
Beat in eggs; incorporate flour, cinnamon, cream and honey.
Beat the mixture thoroughly, then add dissolved saleratus.
Pour into a buttered, paper-lined pan and bake in a slow oven.
note: Faithful paraphrase of the 1855 printed recipe, not a tested modern adaptation. Saleratus is an obsolete leavening agent; do not substitute quantities without a tested conversion.

title: Caraway Seed Cake
author: Ryzon Baking Powder Company
description: A traditional seed cake perfumed with caraway and orange.
method: Cream butter and sugar.
Beat in eggs, then milk, orange extract and caraway seeds.
Fold in flour sifted with the original Ryzon leavening.
Transfer to a buttered and floured small square tin; bake in a moderate oven for about 40 minutes.
note: Paraphrased from the historical source. The exact publication year needs bibliographic confirmation; 1920 is an approximate era label. Ryzon is a historical baking powder brand. Not kitchen-tested.

title: Pavini Cake
book: Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management
author: Isabella Beeton
description: A substantial Victorian fruit-and-rice cake with raisins, currants, almonds and nutmeg.
ingredients: ½ lb raisins, stoned and chopped
method: Stone and chop the raisins; wash and dry the currants.
Cream the butter without letting it become oily; blanch and chop the almonds and grate the nutmeg.
Mix the prepared ingredients thoroughly.
Warm the milk and stir in the carbonate of soda; use it to combine the ingredients into a paste.
Butter a cake mould and fill it a little more than halfway; bake in a moderate oven for 1½–2 hours (less if divided into two cakes).
note: Paraphrased from Mrs. Beeton's 1861 recipe no. 1771. Historical measurements and oven descriptions retained; not kitchen-tested.
reference: Mrs. Beeton, recipe 1771, A Pavini Cake.

title: Tea-Cakes
book: Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management
author: Isabella Beeton
description: Soft, yeast-raised Victorian tea-cakes, served warm with butter; Mrs. Beeton notes optional currants and sugar.
ingredients: A walnut-sized piece of German yeast
Optional: a few currants and sugar
method: Mix the dry flour with salt and rub in the butter or lard.
Beat the egg with the yeast; add to the flour with enough warm milk to form a smooth dough.
Knead well and leave in a warm place to rise.
Shape into eight tea-cakes; place on tins and allow to rise briefly again.
Bake in a moderate oven for 15–30 minutes; serve hot with butter.
note: Paraphrased from Mrs. Beeton's 1861 recipe no. 1786. German yeast is a historical ingredient; no modern conversion is asserted. The previous Russian tea cakes illustration is not an accurate representation.
imageAlt: Small tea cakes; illustrative only, not the exact Victorian recipe

title: Boston Baked Beans
author: Mary Green
description: Slow-baked navy beans with molasses and mustard, a classic New England preparation.
method: Soak beans overnight; drain and simmer in fresh water until tender but intact.
Place in a bean pot with seasonings and scalded, scored salt pork.
Cover with boiling water and bake slowly for eight hours, replenishing water as needed.
Remove the cover for the final hour.
note: Historical recipe paraphrase, not a modern adaptation. Contains pork; the historical version is not vegetarian or vegan. Oven temperature was not specified.

title: Pop-overs
author: Mary Green
description: Crisp, hollow oven-baked batter rolls served warm.
method: Mix the flour and salt.
Add the milk gradually to make a smooth batter.
Beat in the eggs until light, followed by the melted butter.
Beat the batter for two minutes; pour into very hot, buttered iron gem pans.
Bake in a hot oven for 30–35 minutes.
note: The source's ingredient listing has been located, but its full method and remaining ingredient line still require verification. Do not attempt to cook from this partial transcription. title: Susie's Spider Corn Cake
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer
description: An early American skillet-baked corn cake, made with sour milk and baked in a hot oven.
method: Mix the soda, salt and corn meal.
Gradually add well-beaten eggs and sour milk.
Heat a frying pan and grease its bottom and sides with butter.
Pour in the mixture and bake on the middle rack of a hot oven for 20 minutes.
note: Paraphrased from the digitized Boston Cooking-School Cook Book. The linked edition should be checked for its exact publication year; no modern oven temperature is inferred.
